title: Unbounded pagination lets clients bypass the default digest limit
reasoning: The route accepts raw integer query parameters for pagination and passes them directly into SQLAlchemy without lower or upper bounds. In SQLite, `LIMIT -1` means no limit, so an authenticated network client can request `/api/digests?limit=-1` and force the endpoint to load and serialize every digest instead of the documented/default page size. Very large positive limits have the same resource-impact shape.
reproduction: Call `GET /api/digests?limit=-1` against a database with more than 20 digests; the query is built with `.limit(-1)` and returns all matching rows on SQLite.
recommendation: Declare pagination with FastAPI `Query` constraints, for example `limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=100)` and `offset: int = Query(default=0, ge=0)`, choosing a max page size that matches client needs.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The observed digest route test in `tests/test_digest_download_formats.py` only calls `/api/digests` with defaults to verify `available_formats`; no linked or discovered test exercises negative or excessive `limit`/`offset` values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add API tests asserting `GET /api/digests?limit=-1`, `limit=1000000`, and `offset=-1` return 422 or are clamped according to the chosen contract.
minimumFixScope: Update only `list_digests` query parameter declarations and add focused route tests for pagination validation.
